fv_double_population_cap.decision: DECISIONS_2026-11-14 section 6 ("Cap at 8"). The decision record says host worker target; the package uses the coordinator's overall worker target, which on one host has the same effect on leases and leaves the configuration choices alone, and the trigger at most 8 FV primary jobs unfinished, at which point none is waiting to be dispatched. The substitution is stated in the launch package's ask and noted in the decision record
fv_double_population_cap.mechanism: fvd_cap_watch.py, started on X2-1 before the launch and polling each minute: when the coordinator is in phase index 2 and at most 8 of the 834 FV primary jobs are unfinished (826 or more records in validate_fv_primary/records), it runs production_runner control ROOT --workers 8, the overall worker target (multihost_a11.py line 920, enforced on every lease including the phase recheck). The control's transaction lock waits up to 30 s and then raises (multihost_a11.py 122 to 133), so the watcher retries the idempotent control with a growing pause until pull_state.json reads a control.max_workers at or below 8, the pass test, then exits. It reads the target before every attempt, so it never raises a lower target the operator set. If it first sees phase index 3 or later with the target unset, it logs LATE with the running count from each phase's status.json and sets the target at once. It exits also when the launch is complete or its last launch record is finished. It never stops, restarts or drains anything
fv_double_population_cap.liveness: the watcher rewrites a one-line state file (fvd_cap_watch.log.state) every poll and once more at exit with the reason, and survives an error in a poll. It runs under fvd_cap_watch_loop.sh (sha256 8018643ef4b9b3b028a561ce733331aabb1f69509e5fd2109b85507fa8ce037f), which restarts it 60 s after a crash and ends on its intended exits (0) or a failed start precondition (2). The memory watch records its process and the state line's age in every sample. A scheduled interpreter check every 6 hours during the launch reads the state line and the log, and the interpreter checks again when FV primary passes about 700 records, restarting the loop if it has stopped (safe at any time)

At that point no FV primary job is waiting to be dispatched, so the cap costs that phase nothing. The control's transaction lock waits up to 30 s and then raises (multihost_a11.py 122 to 133), so the watcher retries the idempotent control with a growing pause until pull_state.json reads a control.max_workers at or below 8, the pass test, then exits. It reads the target before every attempt, so it never raises a lower target the operator set. If it first sees phase index 3 or later with the target unset, it logs LATE with the running count from each phase's status.json and sets the target at once. It exits also when the launch is complete or its last launch record is finished. It never stops, restarts or drains anything

The other term, 0.8 x MemAvailable, did not bind: the lowest sampled MemAvailable in the phase was 65.4 GB, so the term stayed above 52.3 GB, more than the 22.7 GB that three more leases would have needed. In validate_fv_double_population and census the cap held concurrency at 8 (at most 8 worker processes, means 7.85 and 7.68), against configuration choices of 16 and 24; without it the sheet computed 9 at the double-population open. Each phase's largest recorded peak is below its frozen class. The bound that holds by arithmetic is the recorded peaks': 8 jobs at the phase's largest recorded peak (12.522 GB), all at once, is 100.18 GB, just under the sheet's figure of 8 at sqrt's largest peak (100.19 GB; about 100.2 GB in section 11) and inside the 110 GB GUPPI agreement term. Inferred from the admission rule (section 4) and that count, since no record logs a memory wait: each lease is charged min(max(class, observed), weight). The frozen class is 7.540 GB for all 365 FV primary jobs; the observed term (1.2 x the class's largest recorded peak) reached at most 6.899 GB across the phase's 5 cost classes (pull_state.json observed_memory_gb), below the class; and the weight was 8.878 GB at the open and 9.579 GB with 8 FV primary jobs unfinished (worker_control.top_weighted_counts' rule on the sealed spec's classes, computed on X2-1; validation_segment_stats_x10.json), above the class throughout (inferred from the rule: the weight is the mean of the heaviest quarter of the unfinished reservations, and a finishing FV primary job removes one of its lightest, so it never falls in this phase). So every FV primary lease was charged the class. Against 0.8 x the registered 124.964 GB (99.97 GB), 13 leases fit (98.01 GB) and 14 do not (105.55 GB). The other term, 0.8 x MemAvailable, did not bind: the lowest sampled MemAvailable in the phase was 63.6 GB, so the term stayed above 50.9 GB, more than the 22.6 GB that three more leases would have needed. In validate_fv_double_population and census the cap held concurrency at 8 (means 7.94 and 7.64), against configuration choices of 16 and 24; without it the sheet computed 10 at the double-population open and 11 at census's under d829ff1a (section 4). Each phase's largest recorded peak is below its frozen class and below the crowding validation's: fit 2.770 against 2.936 GB, validate_plain 2.919 against 3.218, validate_fv_primary 5.749 against 6.315, validate_fv_double_population 11.306 against 12.522, census 0.252 against 0.293, from 5.7 to 14.0 percent lower. The sheet had taken crowding's peaks as the reference and said they might read a few percent high here (section 3, inferred). The memory watch samples every 10 s, so its figures can miss a brief coincidence of peaks. Its summed worker RSS was at most 73.0 GB in validate_fv_double_population at 8 workers, above the crowding validation's 70.7 GB at 8 although each job's peak was lower; inferred: here the 16 jobs ran as two waves of 8 (each job 7,018 to 7,734 s in a 4.17 h window), and section 5 of the sheet notes that a wave that starts together can coincide its peaks more than a steady phase. The bound that holds by arithmetic is the recorded peaks': 8 jobs at the phase's largest recorded peak (11.306 GB), all at once, is 90.45 GB, under the sheet's 100.2 GB at crowding's largest peak (section 12) and inside the 110 GB GUPPI agreement term. The host process tree read at most 73.1 GB over the whole run, the configuration tests included; MemAvailable was lowest at 46.8 GB (45,675,764 kB, 2026-11-26T00:55:54Z, validate_fv_double_population, 8 worker processes, summed worker RSS 73.0 GB). Swap free never fell below its value at the go (31,484,372 kB, with about 2.1 GB of swap already in use before the launch; state_at_go.txt) and rose by at most 376 kB. The phases ran one after another with no overlap; the gaps between the last job of one phase and the first of the next were 6.4, 7.0, 24.8, 52.9 minutes, in phase order (the crowding validation's were 6.3, 7.1, 21.4, 53.0). Measured: each of the first four phases' incidental cross-check records (one per phase recheck) falls in the gap after its phase, at most 14.8 s before the next phase's first start, and the next phase projection follows it within 1 s. Between each phase's last completion and its cross-check record every memory-watch sample shows exactly one worker process: 37, 42, 148 and 314 samples in the four gaps, counting a sample only when its whole second lies inside the interval, and 1 in the 9.0 s census interval. After a cross-check record and before the next phase's first record start the samples show no worker process, except one sample: the one at 2026-11-24T21:08:17Z shows 4, 0.79 s before the first validate_fv_primary record's start (inferred: that phase's opening workers; a record's start is its completion less the job's own seconds, so it lags the lease). The session's worker-second total less the 2,132 records' sum is 5,435.4 s, within 3.4 s of the 5,438.8 s that the five intervals from each phase's last completion to its cross-check record add up to. Inferred: the one process is the phase's nondeterminism recheck, run alone, so each gap holds its phase's recheck. Against the sheet's projection (50.78 h, section 7, inferred from the crowding validation's per-phase rates at these job counts, the cap included), the launch wall was 47.92 h, 2.86 h under. By phase, measured wall less projected: fit -0.91 h, validate_plain -2.79, validate_fv_primary +0.66, validate_fv_double_population +0.14, census -0.03; the time outside the five phase windows (the configuration tests at the join, the gaps and the tail) was 2.16 h, against the sheet's 2.10 h. Within a phase the wall is the jobs times the mean job time over the mean concurrency, and the projection took crowding's rate by phase, which is crowding's mean job time over its mean concurrency, so those two terms carry the differences. Mean job time against crowding's: fit 0.809 times, validate_plain 0.808, validate_fv_primary 1.022, validate_fv_double_population 1.047, census 0.913 (medians 0.844, 0.840, 1.039, 0.992 and 0.963); mean concurrency fit 15.79 against 15.88, validate_plain 15.90 against 15.93, validate_fv_primary 12.85 against 12.91, validate_fv_double_population 7.94 against 7.85, census 7.64 against 7.68. Why the job times differ is not separated here. Observations for later load sheets and rate readings, not a capacity binding.
